Note::TexAccessor::strip_color¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_color() const

Remove Color Styling While Retaining Visible Content¶

strip_color() unwraps \textcolor{color}{content}, \colorbox{color}{content}, and \fcolorbox{frame}{background}{content} to their visible content. Optional color-model groups are accepted. Declaration commands \color{...} and \pagecolor{...} are removed because they carry no visible body.

All required and optional groups are balanced, so nested braces in visible content survive. Exact control-word matching prevents longer or escaped commands from being rewritten. An incomplete call remains unchanged rather than exposing only a fragment of its arguments.

Whitespace is collapsed and trimmed after rewriting. The method allocates a new Text Note with the receiver’s rank and shape and does not mutate its input. Undefined state propagates; non-Text dtypes reject. Runtime is linear in source and retained-content bytes.

Example 1: Wrappers, Declarations, And Boundaries¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \textcolor{red}{bold {nested}} B \colorbox{blue}{box} C)",
    R"(\fcolorbox[rgb]{0,0,0}{1,1,1}{framed} \color{green} tail)",
    R"(\\textcolor{red}{escaped} \textcolor{red}{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_color() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A bold {nested} B box C", "framed tail", "\\\\textcolor{red}{escaped} \\textcolor{red}{unfinished"]

Example 2: Declarations, Color Models, And Shape¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\pagecolor{black} white)",
                             R"(\textcolor[rgb]{1,0,0}{red})", "plain", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_color();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "receiver unchanged=" << (grid.at(0).find("pagecolor") != std::string_view::npos)
          << " idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_color()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["white", "red"], 
  ["plain", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
receiver unchanged=true idempotent=true

The optional [rgb] model describes the color argument, not visible content. It disappears with that argument, while the final body remains in place.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_color().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_color();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip color Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip color Int64: rejected
